searchText: it's funny how you could actually see that the next block would have at least one slashing the first block I grabbed had the long range attestation by validator 4100 531-->534 but didn't have the short one 532->533 and surely enough in the next block came the slashing of that validator. Well it looks like that they have turned on their validators again. Side note: The validator that got slashed yesterday #20075 was fine with sharing more information about their setup and was also fine with sharing his username so that interested parties can reach out. I have given it to <@!449019668296892420> and <@!399309815517544451>. can their setup be shared? would love to learn how this happened exactly what is the math, on people running a slasher and saving the proofs for when they propose the next block? could that become a whale play, slashing themselves to collect the rewards on it? This is the tldr on the slashing from yesterday Custom remote signer with multiple independent nodes that make requests to this signer Pubkeys are assigned to nodes and can be duplicated The signer had custom anti slashing logic that did not account for the surround attestation condition One of the nodes was turned off for some time and when it turned back on was out of sync (stale latest justified) So it triggered a surround of another vote from another node making different requests for the same keys . Having multiple nodes think they are in charge of the same keys represents huge risk beyond a more basic setup For the above setup, I would instead recommend having a single VC living next to the keys or being 1:1 with the remote signer. This VC could then load balance across many BNs if desirable Looks like vouch might be written as a VC that can handle this usecase https://www.attestant.io/posts/introducing-vouch/ thanks <@!291925846556540928> do we know how is it that only one entity found all these slashings and was able to store them until they got to be the lucky ones proposing a block? slashings=proofs/offenses so this entity looks to be a large entity on the network and is likely running a slasher that does not broadcast findings other slashers found the slashings but looks like this entity (the one that published the slsahings) was the first one to come up in block proposal selection I think taht only the lighthouse slasher found these slashings and I think that the lighthouse slasher is by default "selfish". Meaning it keeps the slashings for self inclusion in blocks and 500 validators for that entity, landed them such closely spaces proposal opportunities What happens to partial deposits? In principle it's possible to implement a withdrawal after the merge since they hold a valid bls key. Has this been discussed? Partial deposits are just like validators, except they are not activated until they reach 32 eth. Similarly small top-up deposits to existing validators are possible too. In the phase0 time of most validators neither is necessary though, and discouraged if you don't know what you are doing. As it stands, a partial deposit couldn't be withdrawn as it isn't in the correct state. I'd imagine it's not worth trying to fix that, and if someon puts in a 1 Ether deposit and wants it back they'd just have to put in another 31 Ether, work their way through the lifecycle, and withdraw at the end of it.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
Custom remote signer with multiple independent nodes that make requests to this signer
 Pubkeys are assigned to nodes and can be duplicated

The signer had custom anti slashing logic that did not account for the surround attestation condition
One of the nodes was turned off for some time and when it turned back on was out of sync (stale latest justified)

So it triggered a surround of another vote from another node making different requests for the same keys
